introduction: These short passages are addressed by Bahá’u’lláh, and one by the Báb, to the divines, the religious scholars and clergy chiefly of Islam and also the priests of other faiths. They ask them to be fair: to say by what proof they believed before and by what proof they now deny; to still their pens; to cast away what they imagine; and they charge them with pride of learning and with having led the people astray. The prophets of Israel, the Gospels and the Qur’an spoke to priests, scribes and scholars in much the same voice, and those passages are set beside the readings. So are the reasons a conscientious scholar might hesitate, from the command to try the spirits to Paul's warning against any other gospel, and the examples of Nicodemus, Gamaliel and the priests who did believe.
questions: The readings ask the divines by what proof they believed before and by what proof they now deny. What would it be to apply the same standard of evidence to old convictions and new claims?
John's letter tells believers to try the spirits, and Paul curses any other gospel. How can a religious teacher be faithful to such commands and still be open?
Paul says knowledge puffs up; the Qur’an says the learned are those who fear God. What have you seen learning do to people?
Nicodemus asked that a man be heard before he is judged, and Gamaliel advised patience. What part did such voices play, and what part could they play now?
The Grand Inquisitor shows a church defending itself against its own founder. What would keep any religious institution, including one's own, from doing the same?

outside.why: Isaiah promises a day when the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.
Isaiah tells the rulers of his people: seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.
The Qur’an itself teaches the test the readings apply: bring your proof, if ye are truthful.

Deuteronomy gives the learned a test for one who speaks in God's name: if the thing follow not, nor come to pass, the Lord hath not spoken it. What tests may religious scholars fairly apply to a new claim, and how long may they wait?
Jesus said to the scribes of his day: ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men; ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in.
Jesus said: woe unto you, lawyers, for ye have taken away the key of knowledge.
Isaiah says of his people that they draw near with their mouth and honour God with their lips, but have removed their heart far from Him.
Jesus charged the teachers of his day with laying aside the commandment of God to hold the tradition of men.

The first letter of John instructs believers: believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God, because many false prophets are gone out into the world. Is caution toward a new claimant a failing in a religious teacher, or a duty?
Nicodemus asked his fellow Pharisees: doth our law judge any man, before it hear him, and know what he doeth?
In the council Gamaliel, a doctor of the law held in reputation among all the people, stood up and said: take heed to yourselves what ye intend to do as touching these men.
The people of Berea searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.

Paul wrote: though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached, let him be accursed. How does a scholar bound by such a verse judge fairly between what he possesses and what has appeared?

Malachi says that the priest's lips should keep knowledge, and people should seek the law at his mouth, and then: but ye are departed out of the way. What is the proper work of a religious scholar, and when is it betrayed?
Isaiah says that the vision has become as a sealed book, which the learned cannot read because it is sealed, and the unlearned because he is not learned.
Jeremiah asks those who say, we are wise and the law is with us: lo, certainly the pen of the scribes is in vain.
Jesus said that men do not put new wine into old bottles.
Paul asks: where is the wise? where is the scribe? where is the disputer of this world?
The risen Jesus called two of his own disciples slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken.
Jesus said: search the scriptures, for they are they which testify of me, and ye will not come to me.
Habakkuk is told: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come.
The rabbis of the Talmud discouraged calculating the end of days and counselled waiting. What can long expectation do to the readiness of those who teach others to expect?
Jesus said that not every one that saith Lord, Lord shall enter the kingdom, but he that doeth the will of the Father.
The officers sent to seize Jesus came back and said: never man spake like this man.
Isaiah says: O my people, they which lead thee cause thee to err.
The Qur’an says: woe unto those who write the Scripture with their hands and then say, this is from God.
Paul, once a Pharisee of the Pharisees, wrote: I count all things but loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ.
Micah says of the leaders of his day: the priests teach for hire, and the prophets divine for money.
The Qur’an says that many of the rabbis and monks devour the wealth of mankind wantonly and debar men from the way of God.
Paul says that knowledge puffeth up, but charity edifieth, and that whoever thinks he knows anything knows nothing yet as he ought.
The Qur’an says that the erudite among His bondmen fear God alone. What distinguishes the learning that makes a person proud from the learning that makes them humble?
Jeremiah cries: woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture.
Jesus said: they be blind leaders of the blind, and both shall fall into the ditch.
The second letter to Timothy speaks of those ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth.
Isaiah says of the leaders: his watchmen are blind; they are shepherds that cannot understand.
Ezekiel cries: woe be to the shepherds of Israel that do feed themselves; should not the shepherds feed the flocks?

Dostoevsky's Grand Inquisitor tells the returned Christ that the church has corrected his work, and asks why he has come to hinder it. Is the failure these readings describe peculiar to one clergy, or a danger to every religious institution?
The Pharisees asked their officers: have any of the rulers or of the Pharisees believed on him?
The Book of Acts records that in Jerusalem a great company of the priests were obedient to the faith. How should the divines who did recognize a new Messenger be remembered beside those who did not?
Jesus wept over the city, saying: if thou hadst known the things which belong unto thy peace.
Hosea says to the priesthood: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me.
Mary's song says that God hath put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree.

jeremiah-woe-be-unto-the-pastors.text: Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! saith the Lord

isaiah-watchmen-are-blind.text: His watchmen are blind: they are all ignorant, they are all dumb dogs, they cannot bark; sleeping, lying down, loving to slumber. Yea, they are greedy dogs which can never have enough, and they are shepherds that cannot understand: they all look to their own way, every one for his gain, from his quarter

timothy-ever-learning.text: Ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth

acts-gamaliel-take-heed.text: Then stood there up one in the council, a Pharisee, named Gamaliel, a doctor of the law, had in reputation among all the people, and commanded to put the apostles forth a little space; And said unto them, Ye men of Israel, take heed to yourselves what ye intend to do as touching these men

hosea-reject-thee-no-priest.text: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children
